questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design multi-cluster deployment pipelines in Azure DevOps, combining GitOps (Flux) and traditional Helm approaches. It evaluates understanding of per-cluster configuration management, secrets handling, progressive delivery strategies, and observability—all critical skills for production-grade Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Azure DevOps YAML templates with conditional stages and jobs
- Flux GitOps vs Helm deployments in AKS clusters
- Azure App Configuration for feature flags per cluster
- Azure Key Vault secrets integration
- Canary deployments and health checks
- Azure Policy gates and automatic rollback strategies
- Azure Monitor Logs for pipeline observability

## Code Example
```yaml
# azure-pipelines.yml
trigger:
  - main

resources:
  repositories:
    - repository: templates
      type: git
      name: Shared/PipelineTemplates

parameters:
  - name: environments
    type: object
    default:
      - name: dev
        cluster: dev-aks-eastus
        clusterType: flux
      - name: staging
        cluster: staging-aks-eastus
        clusterType: helm
      - name: prod
        cluster: prod-aks-westeu
        clusterType: helm

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndPush
        steps:
          - task: Docker@2
            displayName: Build and push container
            inputs:
              containerRegistry: 'acrConnection'
              repository: 'myapp'
              tag: '$(Build.BuildId)'

  - stage: Deploy_Dev
    dependsOn: Build
    jobs:
      - template: deploy-aks.yml@templates
        parameters:
          environment: dev
          clusterName: dev-aks-eastus
          clusterType: flux
          appConfigName: app-config-dev
          keyVaultName: kv-dev-eastus

  - stage: Deploy_Staging
    dependsOn: Deploy_Dev
    jobs:
      - template: deploy-aks.yml@templates
        parameters:
          environment: staging
          clusterName: staging-aks-eastus
          clusterType: helm
          appConfigName: app-config-staging
          keyVaultName: kv-staging-eastus
      - job: CanaryHealthCheck
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks command invoke \
                  --name staging-aks-eastus \
                  --resource-group rg-staging \
                  --command "kubectl rollout status deployment/myapp"

  - stage: Deploy_Prod
    dependsOn: Deploy_Staging
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployProd
        environment: 'prod'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - template: deploy-aks.yml@templates
                  parameters:
                    environment: prod
                    clusterName: prod-aks-westeu
                    clusterType: helm
                    appConfigName: app-config-prod
                    keyVaultName: kv-prod-westeu
      - job: ProdGate
        dependsOn: DeployProd
        steps:
          - task: AzurePolicy@0
            displayName: Check production policy compliance
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
              policyDefinition: 'prod-aks-policy'
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: Verify health and rollback if failed
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                HEALTH=$(curl -s http://myapp.prod.internal/health)
                if [ "$HEALTH" != "healthy" ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Health check failed"
                  echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=ROLLBACK;isOutput=true]true"
                  exit 1
                fi

  - stage: Monitor
    dependsOn:
      - Deploy_Dev
      - Deploy_Staging
      - Deploy_Prod
    jobs:
      - job: LogToMonitor
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: Log deployment results to Azure Monitor
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'monitorConnection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az monitor app-insights trace show \
                  --app myapp-insights \
                  --analytics "deployment | where timestamp > ago(1h)"
```

```yaml
# deploy-aks.yml (template)
parameters:
  - name: environment
    type: string
  - name: clusterName
    type: string
  - name: clusterType
    type: string
  - name: appConfigName
    type: string
  - name: keyVaultName
    type: string

steps:
  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: 'Fetch App Configuration flags for ${{ parameters.environment }}'
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        az appconfig kv export \
          --name ${{ parameters.appConfigName }} \
          --format json \
          --output-file config.json

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: 'Fetch Key Vault secrets for ${{ parameters.environment }}'
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        az keyvault secret list \
          --vault-name ${{ parameters.keyVaultName }} \
          --query '[].name' \
          -o tsv

  - task: HelmDeploy@0
    displayName: 'Deploy to ${{ parameters.clusterName }}'
    condition: eq('${{ parameters.clusterType }}', 'helm')
    inputs:
      connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      azureResourceGroup: 'rg-aks'
      kubernetesCluster: '${{ parameters.clusterName }}'
      namespace: '${{ parameters.environment }}'
      command: 'upgrade --install'
      chartType: 'FilePath'
      chartPath: 'charts/myapp'
      valueFile: 'charts/myapp/values-${{ parameters.environment }}.yaml'

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: 'Deploy via Flux for GitOps cluster'
    condition: eq('${{ parameters.clusterType }}', 'flux')
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        az aks get-credentials --name ${{ parameters.clusterName }} --resource-group rg-aks
        flux install
        flux create source git myapp \
          --url=https://github.com/org/repo \
          --branch=main
        flux create kustomization myapp \
          --source=myapp \
          --path=clusters/${{ parameters.environment }}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests a practical disaster recovery drill workflow across regions, integrating infrastructure as code, secret management, governance, traffic control, and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-region disaster recovery with Terraform and AKS
- Azure Key Vault per-environment secrets
- Policy-based governance and approvals
- Azure Front Door traffic shaping (canary) and health checks
- Drift detection via Log Analytics and automated rollback
- Auditability and rollback plan

## Code Example

```yaml
# DR drill pipeline sketch (high level)
stages:
- stage: DR
  jobs:
  - job: ProvisionDR
    steps:
    - task: TerraformCLI@0
      inputs:
        command: 'apply'
        workingDirectory: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/terraform/dr'
    - task: AzureKeyVault@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(serviceConnection)'
        KeyVaultName: '$(keyVaultName)'
        SecretsFilter: '*'
    - task: AzureFrontDoor@0
      inputs:
        action: 'update'
        routingRules: |
          - name: 'canary'
            percentage: 10
            backendPool: 'dr-region'
```

## Pipeline Steps

1. **Infrastructure Provisioning**: Deploy DR region resources using Terraform with remote state management
2. **Secret Management**: Retrieve environment-specific secrets from Azure Key Vault using managed identity
3. **Policy Gates**: Implement approval workflows and compliance checks before deployment
4. **Traffic Routing**: Configure Azure Front Door with 10%/90% canary traffic distribution
5. **Health Monitoring**: Deploy Log Analytics queries for drift detection and service health
6. **Automated Rollback**: Configure triggers for automatic failback based on health metrics
7. **Audit Logging**: Enable comprehensive logging across all pipeline stages

## Rollback Plan

- **Immediate Rollback**: Front Door traffic re-routing to primary region (100%)
- **Infrastructure Cleanup**: Terraform destroy DR resources if health checks fail
- **State Restoration**: Restore previous state from remote backend snapshots
- **Incident Documentation**: Generate audit report with root cause analysis

## Why This Question Is Asked
This question assesses practical expertise in deploying multi-tenant SaaS applications with per-tenant routing, gated promotions, and automated rollback capabilities.

## Key Concepts
- Azure DevOps YAML pipelines with per-tenant deployment loops
- Blue/Green deployment topology to App Services across separate resource groups
- Front Door integration for per-tenant traffic routing
- Per-tenant feature flags stored in App Configuration or Key Vault
- Environment approvals and policy gates (Azure Policy + Open Policy Agent)
- ARM template drift detection with automatic rollback to the previous green deployment
- Comprehensive telemetry and logging to Azure Monitor

## Code Example
```yaml
# Azure Pipelines YAML for per-tenant blue/green deployments
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main

parameters:
  - name: tenants
    type: object
    default: []

stages:
  - stage: Deploy_Green
    displayName: 'Deploy to Green Environment'
    jobs:
      - job: Deploy_Tenants
        displayName: 'Deploy Each Tenant'
        pool:
          vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
        steps:
          - checkout: self
          - task: AzureResourceManagerTemplateDeployment@3
            displayName: 'Deploy ARM Template - Green Slot'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              resourceGroupName: '$(greenResourceGroup)'
              location: '$(location)'
              csmFile: '$(template.green.path)'
              overrideParameters: '-tenantIds ${{ parameters.tenants }}'
          - task: AzureAppServiceManage@0
            displayName: 'Swap Green to Production'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              Action: 'Swap Slots'
              WebAppName: '$(webAppName)'
              SourceSlot: 'green'

  - stage: Approval_Gate
    displayName: 'Environment Approval Gate'
    dependsOn: Deploy_Green
    jobs:
      - job: WaitForApproval
        displayName: 'Await Manager Approval'
        pool: server
        timeoutInMinutes: 1440
        steps:
          - task: ManualValidation@0
            timeoutInMinutes: 1440
            inputs:
              notifyUsers: '$(approvalEmail)'
              instructions: 'Approve production traffic shift for ${{ parameters.tenants }}'

  - stage: Policy_Gate
    displayName: 'Policy Validation Gate'
    dependsOn: Approval_Gate
    jobs:
      - job: AzurePolicy_Check
        displayName: 'Azure Policy Compliance Check'
        steps:
          - task: AzurePolicyCheck@0
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              resourceGroupName: '$(greenResourceGroup)'
              policyAssignment: 'security-baseline-compliance'
      - job: OPA_Check
        displayName: 'OPA Policy Gate'
        container: openpolicyagent/opa:latest
        steps:
          - script: |
              opa eval --bundle ./policies --input ./input.json 'data.tenant.deploy_allowed'
            displayName: 'Validate OPA Policy'

  - stage: Traffic_Shift
    displayName: 'Shift Traffic via Front Door'
    dependsOn: Policy_Gate
    jobs:
      - job: Update_FrontDoor
        displayName: 'Update Front Door Routing'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Update Front Door Traffic Weights'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                TENANTS='${{ parameters.tenants }}'
                for tenant in $(echo $TENANTS | tr ',' ' '); do
                  flag=$(az appconfig kv show --name $APP_CONFIG_NAME --key tenant/$tenant/traffic-weight --query value -o tsv)
                  az network front-door routing-rule update --resource-group $(frontDoorRG) --front-door-name $(frontDoorName) --name $tenant --backend-pool-name $(backendPoolName) --weight $flag
                done

  - stage: Drift_Check_Rollback
    displayName: 'Drift Detection and Rollback'
    dependsOn: Traffic_Shift
    condition: failed()
    jobs:
      - job: Detect_Drift
        displayName: 'ARM Template Drift Check'
        steps:
          - task: AzureResourceManagerTemplateDeployment@3
            displayName: 'Run Drift Detection'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              resourceGroupName: '$(greenResourceGroup)'
              deploymentMode: 'Validate'
              csmFile: '$(template.green.path)'
              script: |
                # Check for resource drift
                drift=$(az deployment group what-if --resource-group $(greenResourceGroup) --template-file ./template.json --no-pretty 2>&1)
                if [ ! -z "$drift" ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Drift detected: $drift"
                  exit 1
                fi
      - job: Rollback
        displayName: 'Rollback to Previous Deployment'
        dependsOn: Detect_Drift
        condition: failed()
        steps:
          - task: AzureAppServiceManage@0
            displayName: 'Swap Blue to Production'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              Action: 'Swap Slots'
              WebAppName: '$(webAppName)'
              SourceSlot: 'blue'

  - stage: Monitor
    displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
    jobs:
      - job: Send_Logs
        displayName: 'Publish Pipeline Logs'
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: 'Log to Application Insights'
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: $(azureServiceConnection)
              scriptType: 'bash'
              inlineScript: |
                az monitor app-insights create --resource-group $(appInsightsRG) --app $(appInsightsName)
                az monitor app-insights metrics create --resource-group $(appInsightsRG) --app $(appInsightsName) --metric 'deployment_success' --value 1
```
